units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 1:4">Kil. I, 4</cite> <he>הת׳ והחזרד וכ׳</he> the apple and the crab-apple …, although resembling each other, are heterogeneous (<cite ref="K00674"><he>כִּלְאַיִם</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:5:1">Cant. R. to VIII, 5</cite> <he>מה ת׳ זה עושה וכ׳</he> as the apple tree brings forth fruit in Sivan, so the Law was given in Sivan.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:5:1">Ib.</cite> <he>כל אילן … ות׳ זה מוציא וכ׳</he> every other tree produces first its leaves, and then its fruit (buds), but the apple tree produces its buds first, and then its leaves; even so Israel advanced doing to hearing; <cite ref="Shabbat 88a:8">Sabb. 88ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:3:2">Cant. R. to II, 3</cite>.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:3:2">Ib.</cite> <he>מה ת׳ זה אתה נותן בו איסר וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="A01404"><he>איסור</he></cite>) as the apple, for which you pay an Isar and whose scent you enjoy many times, so &c.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 19:16">Num. R. s. 19<sup>16</sup></cite> (expl. <he>הר ההר</he>, <cite ref="Numbers 20:22">Num. XX, 22</cite>) <he>הר על גבי הר כת׳ קטן על גבי ת׳ גדול</he> a hill upon a hill, like a small apple on a large apple; a. fr.—Pl. <he>תַּפּוּחִים</he>, <he>תַּפּוּחִין</he>.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:5">Cant. R. to II, 5</cite> <he>אלו ההגדות … כת׳</he> that means the Hăgadoth whose flavor and taste are like those of apples.
<cite ref="Menachot 28b:15">Men. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>תַּפּוּחֵי הכרתיים</he>, v. <cite ref="K01285"><he>כְּרֵתִי</he></cite>; a. fr.—2) (from its shape)

senses.gloss: ת׳ עקב the fleshy part of the heel. Pesik. Par., p. 36ᵇ ת׳ עקיבו וכ׳ the apple of Adam’s heel outshone the globe of the sun; ib. Aḥăré, p. 170ᵃ; Lev. R. s. 20; a. e.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: pile, esp. the place on the altar where the ashes were piled up.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 4:8">Ab. Zar. IV, 8</cite> <he>אע״פ … ונותן לת׳</he> although the gentile may take grapes in his hand and put them on the pile.
Tam. II, 2 החלו … ע״ג ת׳ והת׳ היה וכ׳ they began to put the ashes on the tappuaḥ, and the t. was in the centre of the altar, containing at times as much as &c.; Ḥull. 90ᵇ.
Ib. חולצו לת׳ he takes it (the nervus ischiadicus) out, and throws it on the tappuaḥ; a. e.
